title: UNIT 1: BIOLOGY AND TECHNOLOGY
notes: ✓ The combination of biology and technology produces biotechnology, which uses biological systems to develop useful products and services.

title: 1.1 LEARNING FROM NATURE
notes:
✓ Nature provides ideas, structures and mechanisms that inspire scientists and engineers to design technologies.

✓ Swallow nests → house-building ideas.
✓ Spider webs → weaving technology.
✓ Termite mounds → buildings with natural temperature and humidity control.
✓ Birds and bats → aircraft wings and flight technology.
✓ Human eye → camera design.
✓ Kangaroo movement → bio-robots.
✓ Mosquito proboscis → injection needles.
✓ Biological neurons → electronic sensors.
✓ Animal teeth → cutting saws.
✓ Spider silk → synthetic bulletproof materials.
✓ Shellfish exoskeleton → crack-resistant ceramics.
✓ Elephant trunk → robotic arms.
✓ Kingfisher beak → bullet-train nose design.

✓ Biomimicry = designing technology by imitating nature.

title: 1.2 BIOLOGY AND TECHNOLOGY
notes:
✓ Biotechnology = integration of biology and technology to develop useful products, methods and services.

✓ Example → yeast is used to produce bread and alcoholic beverages.

title: 1.2.1 BENEFITS OF BIOLOGY TO TECHNOLOGY
notes:
✓ Medicinal plants → natural compounds used to develop medicines.

✓ Gene engineering → biological genes used to develop useful products and help address genetic conditions.

✓ Biosynthetic materials → materials developed to repair damaged body tissues.

✓ Termite architecture → buildings with improved temperature and humidity control.

✓ Kingfisher beak → efficient bullet-train design.

✓ Nature acts as a model for solving engineering and human problems.

title: 1.2.2 USES OF TECHNOLOGY IN BIOLOGY
notes:
✓ Thermometer → measures body temperature.

✓ Pregnancy test → detects pregnancy.

✓ Diabetic blood test → measures blood glucose.

✓ HIV test → detects HIV infection.

✓ Microscope → magnifies small objects and organisms.

✓ CT scan → produces detailed X-ray images for disease detection.

✓ PET scan → shows metabolic and physiological activity using radioactive tracers.

✓ GPS → collects geographical/biogeographical information about landscapes, organisms and movements.

✓ Body-fat calculator → estimates body-fat level.

✓ Technology makes biological observation, measurement, diagnosis and investigation more accurate and efficient.

title: 1.3.2 IMPACTS OF TECHNOLOGY ON SOCIETY & NATURE
notes:
✓ Technology solves many human problems but can also damage the environment when poorly designed or misused.

✓ Major negative impacts:
✓ Industrial emissions → air pollution.
✓ Industrial effluents → water pollution.
✓ Pesticides and fertilizers → toxicity and biohazards.
✓ Industrialization → depletion of natural resources.
✓ Improper technological use → environmental degradation.

✓ Sustainable technology aims to meet human needs while reducing environmental damage.

title: 1.4 ETHICAL ISSUES IN BIOLOGY
notes:
✓ Biological ethics deals with deciding what is right or wrong when using biological knowledge, technologies and discoveries.

✓ Important concerns include:
✓ Human health and safety.
✓ Environmental protection.
✓ Biotechnology and medical practices.
✓ Human rights and equality.
✓ Commercialization of human organs.
✓ Assisted reproduction.
✓ Manipulation of biological systems.

✓ Ethical biology → respect life, rights, dignity, equality and the environment.

title: 1.4.1 ETHICAL TREATMENT OF PLANTS & ANIMALS
notes: ✓ Biological studies involving plants and animals should minimize unnecessary damage, suffering and destruction.

title: 1.4.1.2 ETHICAL TREATMENT OF ANIMALS IN EXPERIMENTS
notes:
✓ Animals are sentient organisms capable of experiencing pain and stress. Research should therefore minimize suffering and unnecessary use of animals.

✓ Three Rs principle:
✓ Reduction → use the minimum number of animals necessary.

✓ Refinement → improve procedures and living conditions to reduce pain and suffering.

✓ Replacement → use alternatives such as cell cultures, biosynthetic tissues or computer models instead of animals when possible.

title: UNIT 1 QUICK REVISION
notes:

✓ Biomimicry → imitation of nature in technology.
✓ Biology + Technology → Biotechnology.
✓ Biology → provides natural models and biological knowledge.
✓ Technology → provides tools for biological investigation.
✓ CT/PET → medical imaging.
✓ GPS → biological/geographical data collection.
✓ Biology & technology → positive + negative impacts.
✓ Ethics → right and responsible use of biological knowledge.
✓ Plant ethics → conservation and responsible use.
✓ Animal ethics → minimize suffering.
✓ 3 Rs → Reduction + Refinement + Replacement.
